answers.reasoning: Current is carrier drift; bulk wire motion is not needed for magnetic force.
The vector product v cross B vanishes for parallel vectors.
Commutation changes coil-current direction to keep the torque sense through the next half-turn.
V_b/omega has units V per rad/s; rpm/V is its reciprocal-type speed convention, not the stated constant.
Internal friction requires positive electromagnetic torque even with zero useful external shaft load.
The high unloaded speed warning requires appropriate loading and speed protection, not reliance on current limiting alone.
Shunt field current24/120=.2A plus armature current(24-20)/2=2A gives2.2A.
At fixed flux and supply, increased armature drop leaves less back EMF and slightly lower speed.
At fixed K_t, I_a=T/K_t is linear despite the source curved sketch.
The displayed table says shunt high, series low and compound parallel high/series low.
Current controls torque, but speed also needs the voltage/back-EMF equation and mechanical load equilibrium.
Continuous left-to-right inductive current follows ground to lower-left diode, winding, upper-right diode, then absorbing positive rail; left is0V and right24V, so power vi=-48W.
Measured speed1.6/.02=80rad/s, leaving target-minus-measurement20rad/s.
A block diagram and static feedback sign alone cannot establish closed-loop stability with arbitrary gain and delay.
Three sensors describe sensored commutation, while sensorless schemes estimate position from measured electrical signals.
Synchronous mechanical speed is electrical frequency divided by the pole-pair count.
The induction statement must be scoped to induction machines, not permanent-magnet synchronous rotors.
One pole pair at50Hz is50revolutions/s, or3000rpm.
Total pulses set steps/displacement; their temporal rate sets nominal speed when all are followed.
360/144=2.5degrees; the other step-count/angle pairs do not multiply to360.
Below the intersection motor torque exceeds load, giving acceleration; above it the sign reverses.
The two source generalizations have different contexts and do not supply current measured market shares.
Currents6A and2A give72W and8W; duration-weighted mean(72*2+8*6)/8=24W.
Ideal unloaded omega=V/K_v and fixed-torque I=T/K_t both double when their respective constants halve; these are separate operating comparisons.
